opening.argument: The video presents Routine founders explaining an ordinary natural-deodorant business: they discuss convincing people to try the product, the company’s growth, and a past cash-flow difficulty. Their financing account concerns the founders’ own contribution and conventional business borrowing: they say, “So initially we each put $250 into the company, and we bootstrapped our way” and that they “worked with the bank to secure a loan.” Nothing in this discussion asks viewers to invest, pay money, or provide private information. The sampling and event context likewise support routine product promotion and commerce, while the cash-flow discussion is presented as business history rather than a solicitation or promised opportunity.
